assumptions: Each level's assembly follows its chemistry's own simulation.
limits: Errors compound across levels; a level with no product stops the plan, and it says where.
bio.jane/contract.question: What final construct does a multi-level assembly plan give, each level's products becoming the next level's parts?

description: Run a MULTI-LEVEL assembly plan (DnaCauldron `AssemblyPlan`): several assemblies arranged into dependency levels, where each level's products become parts for the next. Emits the FINAL construct as a record. The plan is DnaCauldron's own spreadsheet shape — one row per construct, `construct_name, part, part, …`.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

include_subject.description: also offer the node's subject as a part.

method.description: the assembly chemistry every step uses (upstream passes one class per spreadsheet). Values: type2s (Golden Gate (Type-IIS)), gibson (Gibson / homologous), biobrick (BioBrick standard), basic (BASIC (linker-based)), lcr (Ligase cycling reaction), annealing (Oligo pair annealing).

parts.description: the physical parts — wire upstream `record` outputs here, or list library document names/ids. A part is addressed by this NAME in the plan rows.

plan.description: the plan, in DnaCauldron's spreadsheet shape: one line per construct, `name,partA,partB`. A construct name may itself be used as a part in a later line — that is what makes the plan multi-level.

name: assembly_plan_simulate

cancelled.description: steps never attempted because a dependency failed

constructs.description: every construct produced, in build order

leafParts.description: the physical parts a bench user must actually have

levels.description: the derived build order: which steps happen at which level

record.description: the final construct (deepest level), as a record
